newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl - Bonn will not accept delay in EMU timetable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl - Bonn will not accept delay in EMU timetable.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Friday for the first time categorically ruled out a delay in the start of European monetary union, reaffirming that Germany would meet all the entry criteria.
"Germany will never accept a delay in the timetable," he said. "Under no circumstances."
"Germany will completely fulfil the criteria," he added.
Kohl was speaking to industrialists in Duesseldorf.
A delay in the start of EMU has been proposed by some given the problems many nations are facing in meeting the strict entry criteria for the monetary union.
Countries which wish to enter monetary union in 1999 must meet targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, total debt and public deficits this year.

For most countries, the deficit requirement, which calls for a deficit level of no more than three percent of domestic product, is proving the hardest to meet. Germany is aiming for a 2.9 percent level this year, which many see as optimistic.
On public debt, the ideal target is 60 percent of GDP. Countries with much higher debt levels must at least show that they are making progress toward that level.

Germany is currently running a debt level of just over 60 percent which is set to rise this year, but has already pleaded that the special situation of German unification should warrant it special treatment in the final assessment.
